title: Risk-based credibility assessment of explicit FEA models for deployment force in a transcatheter delivery system under ASME V&V 40
device: Transfemoral transcatheter delivery system for a self-expanding valve

models.name: Model-HF
models.what_it_computes: High-fidelity 3D explicit finite element analysis of the delivery system, computing time-resolved actuator force during unsheathing and partial release, including detailed contact, large deformation, and frictional stick–slip.

models.name: Model-RO
models.what_it_computes: Reduced-order explicit FE submodel with homogenized device and sheath representation, computing deployment-force envelopes and peak force estimates under prescribed kinematics.

mechanisms.name: Unsheathing friction and stick–slip
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Peaks in handle force during sheath retraction can cause loss of positional control, abrupt release, or tissue injury.

mechanisms.name: Frame recoil constraint during staged release
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Stored elastic energy in the self-expanding frame generates reaction forces transmitted through the handle; excessive force can lead to overshoot and malposition.

clear_factors: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

deviation.detail: All credibility factor ratings are reported on a 0–5 Credibility Index (CI), with critical factors requiring CI ≥ 4.0 and non-critical factors requiring CI ≥ 3.5.

sections: Context of use and model risk: The models are intended to inform design verification and preclinical evidence by predicting operator handle force during deployment; decision is whether design variants meet an internal deployment-force limit. Model risk: high — rationale: an incorrect prediction could contribute to device malposition or vascular injury; clinical decision could be negatively influenced if nonconforming designs are released.
Device and mechanisms: Transfemoral delivery system architecture and two deployment-force mechanisms (unsheathing friction; frame recoil constraint)
Computational models: Explicit FEA formulations, discretization strategies, contact and friction modeling, and primary output (deployment force time histories and peaks)
Risk-informed credibility plan and acceptance criteria (0–5 Credibility Index; critical factors: Numerical code verification, Numerical solver error, Output comparison)
Numerical code verification: methodology and outcomes across models and mechanisms
Numerical solver error: time-step sensitivity, mass scaling audits, and energy balance across models and mechanisms
Output comparison: bench rig measurements of deployment force vs. model outputs, comparison metrics, and pass/fail against predefined tolerances
Relevance of the validation activities to the COU: alignment of test conditions, kinematics, and boundary conditions with intended clinical use
Software quality assurance: configuration management, peer review, and defect tracking for pre- and post-processors and the FE solver
Test samples: selection, representativeness, and coverage of device sizes and sheath lubricity states
Use error considerations: operator training notes and procedural consistency (noted)
Synthesis of factor scores (0–5 CI) — Pair 1: Model-HF × Unsheathing friction — code verif 4.5; solver error 3.8; output comparison 3.6; relevance 4.2; SQA 4.0; test samples 3.5; use error noted
Synthesis of factor scores (0–5 CI) — Pair 2: Model-HF × Frame recoil constraint — code verif 4.5; solver error 4.1; output comparison 2.9; relevance 3.8; SQA 4.0; test samples 3.0; use error noted
Synthesis of factor scores (0–5 CI) — Pair 3: Model-RO × Unsheathing friction — code verif 3.7; solver error 3.3; output comparison 3.1; relevance 3.9; SQA 3.5; test samples 2.8; use error noted
Synthesis of factor scores (0–5 CI) — Pair 4: Model-RO × Frame recoil constraint — code verif 3.5; solver error 2.9; output comparison 2.4; relevance 3.5; SQA 3.5; test samples 2.5; use error noted

Decision and implications: Multiple critical factors failed to meet CI ≥ 4.0, notably Output comparison and Numerical solver error; therefore the models are not accepted for the stated context of use.
